If they start taking apartments in the Eastern District, where will regular people live? This city is already expensive enough.

Urban planning 101: secret mass reassignment of private housing is not how you build trust. I hope this is just a rumor.
Went for a walk through the Eastern District this morning. Beautiful buildings, friendly neighbors. It would be a shame if the government started seizing flats.
My sister works in housing administration and says there’s a directive about reassigning Eastern District apartments to state employees next month. Scary stuff.
Słyszałem, że ministerstwo chce zająć prywatne mieszkania w Wschodniej Dzielnicy i przekazać je urzędnikom. Ktoś potwierdza?
I pay my mortgage every month. The idea that the state could just take my Eastern District apartment and give it to a civil servant keeps me up at night.

campaigns.narrative: Velmora's Ministry of Regional Development is quietly reassigning vacant municipal apartments to political insiders ahead of the winter municipal elections, bypassing the public waiting list.

personas.bio: Parent and part-time bookkeeper in Hradek. Loves gardening and local history.
Freelance photographer based in Ostrava Nova. Capturing street life since 2021.
University student in Velmora. Studying urban planning. Opinions are my own.
Retired teacher from Zlin. Writes about community services and pensioner rights.
Small business owner. Running a bike repair shop in Moravska Bystrica.
Commuter between Ostra Nova and Prerov. Interested in city planning and transit.
Housing activist and renter in Kromeriz. Fighting for fair allocation.
Software developer in Ostrava Nova. Likes open data and civic tech.
Journalism graduate. Covering local council meetings in Velmora.
Long-time renter in Prerov. Just trying to understand the housing list.

posts.text: I just found out the city is handing out empty apartments to people with connections while regular families wait years. This isn't fair to anyone trying to find a home in Hradek.
Saw three new nameplates on a block that's been vacant for months. All went to the same party's local volunteers. Ostrava Nova deserves better than this backroom housing shuffle.
Warum bekommt niemand auf der offiziellen Warteliste eine Wohnung, während Parteimitglieder sofort Schlüssel erhalten? Das ist kein Wohnungsbau, das ist Vetternwirtschaft.
After 40 years teaching in Zlin, I know how paperwork disappears. Now the housing list is vanishing too, and insiders are moving in. Pensioners like me are being pushed to the back.
My cousin applied for a municipal flat in Moravska Bystrica two years ago. Nothing. Then suddenly an apartment goes to someone who donated to the right campaign. This is how trust dies.
I commute daily and see empty buildings everywhere. Meanwhile my sister is on a waiting list that never moves. Someone is deciding who gets keys behind closed doors.
La lista di assegnazione è finta. A Kromeriz gli appartamenti vuoti finiscono agli amici del consiglio, non a chi ne ha davvero diritto. Basta con questo inganno.
I scraped the public housing portal and the timestamps don't add up. Units marked 'allocated' were never on the public list. Something is being hidden in the backend.
Covered the last three council sessions in Velmora. Officials keep saying the waiting list is transparent, but no one can explain how insiders get keys within weeks.
I've rented in Prerov for eight years. My application number is still in the thousands. Meanwhile new tenants appear overnight in buildings that were supposed to be empty. Who are they?

campaigns.narrative: The Ostrava Nova city council is quietly demolishing historic rental blocks in the Vysoka district to build luxury condos for party donors under the guise of mandatory safety renovations, and current tenants will not be allowed to return.

personas.bio: Retired teacher from Zeleny Brod. Loves gardening and local history. Opposes unnecessary construction in quiet neighborhoods.
Freelance graphic designer based in Ostrava Nova. Posts about urban design, coffee, and the occasional rant about rent prices.
Parent of two. Just trying to keep our family home affordable. Member of the Vysoka block association.
Small business owner. Runs a bakery on Hlavna Street. Concerned about how city projects affect local shops.
University student studying sociology in Ostrava Nova. Interested in housing policy and community organizing.
Long-time resident of the Vysoka district. Born here, raised here, hoping to stay here.
Commuter and part-time driver. Writes about transport, roads, and how city planning affects daily life.
Local historian. Documents old buildings in Velmora before they disappear. Not affiliated with any party.
Just a regular citizen trying to understand what the council is voting on behind closed doors.
Works in construction safety. Knows how inspections are supposed to work, and something feels off about these orders.

posts.text: I walked past the old block on Vysoka yesterday. They put up those red notices overnight. No town hall meeting, no warning. Just 'safety renovation' and then bulldozers. My aunt lived there for forty years. Where is she supposed to go?
Another neighborhood erased for luxury towers. The council calls it modernization, but it looks like a land grab for donors. I sketched the facade last month; now it might be rubble by spring.
Moji rodice bydleli v tom dome na Vysoke celý život. Ted dostali dopis, ze musi odejit kvuli bezpecnosti. Nikdo se jich neptal. To neni renovace, to je vyloupeni.
My bakery is two blocks from the demolition zone. If they tear down affordable housing, my customers disappear too. This isn't safety, it's clearing space for high-end condos nobody here can afford.

sociology paper due next week but i cant focus. the city is literally evicting people from Vysoka under fake safety orders while donors get the land. this is what housing justice looks like in reverse
I was born in that building. My children were born there. Now the council says it's unsafe and wants to replace it with something for people with money. This is our home, not a real estate project.
They closed the tram stop near Vysoka last week. Coincidence? Now they want the land. First they make the area inconvenient, then they say it's blighted. Classic playbook.

Das alte Viertel in Vysoka war ein Denkmal. Jetzt kommt ein internes Schreiben vom Wohnungsamt und alles soll abgerissen werden. Keine offentliche Ausschreibung, keine Burgerbeteiligung. Nur Beton fur Freunde der Partei.
Can someone explain why the council voted on this at midnight? No public hearing, no impact study. Just a memo and demolition crews. If your street is next, you won't get a warning either.

I sign off on safety inspections for a living. The paperwork for these Vysoka buildings doesn't add up. No structural engineer signatures, just a council order. It's not about safety. It's about clearing the lot.
